goal: Continue replacing the remaining amateur elements of the 3D island with authored, properly licensed assets and materials, in this priority order: (1) value/atmosphere — the castle stone is too pale and the horizon is a white haze band that flattens all depth; darken and warm the stone, pull the fog back and tint it by height so the castle reads as a dark mass against a bright sky; (2) path and ground treatment — authored path edges with gravel scatter, worn verges, grass density falling off into bare earth beside the track; (3) terrain zoning — rock outcrops and dirt/scree patches breaking the meadow, vegetation density tied to zone so the landscape reads as sculpted rather than one uniform lawn; (4) character silhouette and outfit. Replace weak elements rather than tuning them. Each iteration must produce art-review/after.png from scripts/art-shot.mjs and update art-review/change-report.md. Hard rules: never weaken, skip or delete a test; never loosen the thresholds in scripts/ui-gate.mjs or scripts/visual-gate.mjs; any change to the perf budget must be justified in-file and reported; every third-party asset must be CC0 or permissively licensed and recorded in ASSET_LICENSES.md with author, license, URL and where it is used; no ripped Nintendo, Ghibli or commercial-game assets.
_note: The following do NOT count as a visual iteration on their own: changing hex colours, increasing grass count, adding primitive geometry, changing fog distance alone, raising shadow resolution, adjusting bloom, adding noise, tweaking roughness, adding comments about future work, or the build merely passing. The command gate proves the substrate (install, build, tests, page load, no console errors, screenshot generation, required files exist); the human gate is the only thing that can judge whether the art actually improved. No LLM rubric is used as the final visual gate.

command_gate.command: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && pnpm test && node scripts/visual-gate.mjs && node scripts/ui-gate.mjs && node scripts/art-shot.mjs art-review/after.png && test -f art-review/before.png && test -f art-review/after.png && test -f art-review/change-report.md && test -f ASSET_LICENSES.md

human_gate.prompt: Compare art-review/before.png and art-review/after.png. Approve only if the castle, terrain, and vegetation have been visibly replaced rather than incrementally adjusted, and the result looks materially closer to a polished indie-game portfolio piece. Reject if it still resembles a beginner Three.js tutorial.
human_gate.evidence_hint: open art-review/before.png and art-review/after.png side by side, then read art-review/change-report.md
